name: Cefalexin (Cephalexin)
executiveSummary: 1st-generation oral cephalosporin. Adult: **250–500 mg q6h** (up to **1 g q6h** severe; max **4 g/day**). Pediatrics: **25–50 mg/kg/day** q6h (severe **50–100 mg/kg/day**, max **3 g/day**).
indications:
## Indications

- Skin/soft-tissue, UTI, streptococcal pharyngitis (alternative), oral step-down osteomyelitis.
- Selected dental endocarditis prophylaxis schemes.

## Precautions

- Possible cross-allergy with penicillins (low but real).
- Adjust in severe renal impairment. No MRSA, anaerobes, or Pseudomonas coverage.

> Oral only — no IV cefalexin presentation.

adulto.dose: Usual: **250–500 mg PO q6h**. More severe: **500 mg–1 g q6h** (max **4 g/day**). Uncomplicated UTI: often **500 mg q12h**. Endocarditis prophylaxis (if indicated): **2 g PO 30–60 min before**.
adulto.administration: PO; with or without food (food ↓ nausea).

pediatrico.dose: **25–50 mg/kg/day** divided q6h (or q8–12h per label). Severe: **50–100 mg/kg/day** (max **3 g/day**). Otitis/skin: often **25–50 mg/kg/day**.
pediatrico.notes: Chronic UTI prophylaxis: weigh resistance risk.

neonatal.dose: Guide **25–50 mg/kg/day** divided; UTI prophylaxis <2 mo sometimes **10–15 mg/kg at night** — specialist only.
neonatal.notes: Severe neonatal infection: prefer IV (other cephalosporins).

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted suspension: refrigerate per label (often 7–14 days).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Diarrhea, nausea, thrush, rash; rare: C. difficile colitis, hepatitis, neutropenia.
